title: Formal Correctness Bound for JPEG-Tolerant Image Encryption
summary: The paper reports empirical correctness tests for particular similarity and JPEG-tolerance choices, but a formal correctness bound for the pipeline remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Fix an image-similarity predicate $\mathsf{Similar}$, JPEG-tolerance parameters $r_l$ and $r_r$, and the preprocessing and correction/filtering postprocessing of the JPEG-tolerant stream-cipher image-encryption pipeline. Prove an explicit $\varepsilon$-correctness bound showing that, after an image $I$ is encrypted, its ciphertext is JPEG-compressed, and the result is decrypted and postprocessed to produce $\widehat I$, one has $\mathsf{Similar}(I,\widehat I)$ with probability at least $1-\varepsilon$. Correctness for particular choices of $\mathsf{Similar}$, $r_l$, and $r_r$ has been tested empirically but lacks a formal argument. A proof should account for the intended preservation of closeness through JPEG compression and stream-cipher decryption, possible bit-flipping noise, and the noise reduction supplied by preprocessing and correction.

scope.domain: The problem concerns a JPEG-tolerant stream-cipher image-encryption pipeline with preprocessing and correction/filtering postprocessing.
assumptions: an image-similarity predicate Similar is fixed
the preprocessing and correction/filtering postprocessing are fixed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Provide a formal argument for the explicit epsilon-correctness bound after JPEG compression, decryption, and postprocessing, accounting for closeness preservation, bit-flipping noise, and noise reduction from preprocessing and correction.

progress.summary: The paper explicitly states that it cannot formally argue correctness and instead empirically tests particular choices of Similar, r_l, and r_r, deferring the discussion to Section 10. It motivates the gap through intended closeness preservation under compression and decryption, possible bit-flipping noise, and mitigation through preprocessing and correction.
